overview: Kliker Blocks is a visual Windows scenario editor. Connect blocks for conditions, loops, input, files and screenshots. Run from the editor, compact panel or tray. Select a topic on the left or search by block, function or parameter. Version 0.72 gives Run file a searchable installed-program list and file browser. The demo uses its own Notepad document even when Notepad is already open and verifies the active tab before typing. Translation blocks need a separately running service or optional offline models installed after confirmation; the demo does not translate text.

sections.\u041F\u0430\u043D\u0435\u043B\u044C, \u: Closing the editor opens the compact Kliker Blocks panel. Run, pause, resume or stop the current scenario there, and reopen the editor. Closing the panel hides it in the system tray; use Exit Kliker Blocks in the panel or tray menu to quit. Each instance has its own tray icon: green means running, yellow paused, gray ready. Pausing is cooperative: an action already in progress finishes before execution waits. Kliker Blocks releases held keys and buttons at a safe pause boundary.
sections.\u0417\u0430\u043F\u0443\u0441\u043A \u0: A scenario starts at its single Start block. Select one pass or repeat from the beginning until stopped. Run from the Scenario menu, compact panel, tray, or Ctrl+Alt+F6. Stop there or with Ctrl+Alt+F7; pause from the menu, panel or tray. An unconnected output ends its branch. A backward connection creates a loop.
sections.\u0414\u0435\u043C\u043E\u043D\u0441\u04: The What I can do menu opens an interactive graph. It types and verifies text in Notepad, asks questions, draws your chosen shape in Paint, finds a selected color, and reports the results. Translation is deliberately excluded because the lightweight edition does not bundle Python or language models. On a retry, the demo undoes earlier strokes and selects the drawing tool again. If the old Windows Beep API is unavailable, the sound-signal block uses normal Windows audio. Each new Kliker Blocks version offers the demo again; desktop actions still require consent. Esc or Stop interrupts later actions but leaves opened windows and files. The clipboard changes. Do not run it over sensitive content.
sections.\u041E\u043A\u043D\u0430 \u0438 \u0442\u: When space allows, Notepad is placed left of the graph. The entire document is copied and verified, not just a visually wrapped line. Missed characters are corrected through the clipboard and verified again. Paint starts with a blank canvas; Kliker Blocks locates the pencil and red color, measures the visible white area and draws inside it with mouse input. If the interface cannot be recognized or no strokes appear, the demo reports an error. Classic Paint was not available on the test computer for a live integration test.
sections.\u0412\u0438\u0437\u0443\u0430\u043B\u04: Add blocks from the Blocks menu or left palette. Drag an output connector to the next block's input. An output has one link; an input can have many. Shift+left drag selects an area; Ctrl+C/V copies and pastes selected blocks. Delete removes the selected block or link. Drag empty canvas to pan; Ctrl+wheel zooms. Edit the selected block in the right-hand properties panel.
sections.\u0422\u0435\u043A\u0441\u0442\u043E\u04: Use Blocks / Kliker Blocks code above the canvas to edit the same graph as text, including cycles and parallel links. Syntax: block <label> <type> <X> <Y> [id <GUID>], followed by value "Field" = "Value" and link "Output" -> <label> or none, then end. trace true enables per-block journal entries. A new block can omit id; keep existing GUIDs when editing. Apply code validates the entire text before changing the graph.
sections.\u041F\u0435\u0440\u0435\u043C\u0435\u04:
User variable and array names contain only A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and _. The first character must be a letter or _: counter, total_2, _flag are valid; 2total and my-value are not. Names are case-insensitive. Check names with Languages → Check project variable names.

Set variable creates or replaces a value; Define variable only creates it if missing. Math variable changes a numeric value, starting from 0 if missing. If variable selects Yes/No. Undefine also removes the array of the same name. Values are stored as strings; arithmetic needs numeric input.

Use ${counter} to interpolate into a field. A field beginning with = is evaluated as an expression, for example =($counter+2)*3 or =$counter>=10 and $enabled. Use $counter, not ${counter}, inside expressions. Array items are $items[0]; arrsize($items) returns size and arrpop($items) removes the last item. Indices start at 0.

Variables are shared by blocks, subroutines and parallel branches within one run. They persist between passes of a repeating scenario but reset on a new run; current values are not saved in .klb. Parallel writes to the same name have no defined order. System values include $_xmouse, $_ymouse, $_time_h, $_time_m, $_time_s, $_date_y, $_date_m, $_date_d, $_time_str, $_date_str, $_time_t, $_ms, $_xmin, $_ymin, $_xmax and $_ymax. Do not log secrets.
sections.\u0416\u0443\u0440\u043D\u0430\u043B \u0:
Each block has a Log actions checkbox. When enabled, completion adds its name, short ID and chosen output to the execution journal; errors are logged too. Explicit messages and Kliker Blocks diagnostics appear regardless. In graph code use trace true.

Scenario → Write journal to text file records the full current run, including diagnostics and selected block actions. Enter a .txt/.log filename without a path. The file is created at run start beside a saved .klb, or beside Kliker.Blocks.exe for an unsaved project; its full path is shown in settings and the on-screen journal. UTF-8 output is appended across runs, up to 8 MiB. This project setting does not clear the file when the on-screen journal is cleared. The separate Log file block/#logfile creates its file when reached but writes explicit scenario messages only. Avoid recording passwords or tokens.
sections.\u0421\u043D\u0438\u043C\u043A\u0438 \u0: The Capture menu saves a point, captures a chosen screen region, and opens the image library. Choose the region shape while capturing. In image-search blocks select a saved template, bounds and tolerance. Subsequent blocks can use the found coordinates.
sections.\u0417\u0430\u043F\u0438\u0441\u044C \u0: The Macro menu offers full action recording and click recording with image templates. The recorder panel can pause, resume and stop recording. Save the result in the library and convert it to editable blocks.
sections.\u0421\u043B\u0435\u0436\u0435\u043D\u04: Watch cursor can start immediately, toggle with a key, or work while a key is held. It may additionally require the left, right or middle mouse button or another key. Configure anchor, movement threshold, return target, polling interval and delay. Applications may handle mouse input differently; bypassing protection is not supported.
sections.\u0418\u043D\u0434\u0438\u043A\u0430\u04: The always-on-top indicator shows scenario and tracking states. In the Scenario menu choose its position, shape, size, colors or images for each state, captions and show/hide hotkey. Each Kliker Blocks instance has its own indicator and project settings.
sections.\u041F\u0440\u043E\u0444\u0438\u043B\u04: Open Mouse mappings → Profiles, layers and buttons. Create a profile and enable mappings. Profiles are checked top to bottom; All windows is the fallback. Match the active or hovered window by process, title, class or a rectangle relative to its top-left corner. Empty match fields impose no restriction. Each profile has 1–10 layers. Add mappings from a button/wheel event and trigger mode to an action. Supported triggers include press, release, hold, repeat, toggle, chord, short press and up to four long-press thresholds. Key actions accept Ctrl+C or sequences such as Ctrl+C, 100ms, Ctrl+V. Block original suppresses the source event; the wheel supports individual scroll events only. Ctrl+Alt+F8 toggles mappings; holding Ctrl+Alt temporarily passes the original mouse input through. Mappings pause over Kliker Blocks windows. Two instances can run scenarios concurrently, but enable mouse remapping in only one to avoid duplicate actions. Some applications may ignore synthetic Windows input.
sections.\u041F\u0435\u0440\u0435\u0432\u043E\u04: Languages → Interface language and translation models selects RU/EN/FR/ES/ZH, a Python executable with argostranslate, and an optional LibreTranslate URL. Changing language recreates the interface automatically, retaining unsaved project data in memory. Translate text supports LibreTranslate /translate (source auto is allowed) or Local Argos (explicit source language and installed model required). Detect language uses /detect; If translation available uses /languages. These two blocks require a running LibreTranslate server. Translate array processes array entries through the chosen engine. ${source_text} substitutes a variable. A remote service receives the text you send to it. Detailed help in EN is built in; FR/ES/ZH require a local ru → target model for full topic text. Translation quality depends on the model; a custom terminology dictionary is not yet provided.
sections.\u0423\u0441\u0442\u0430\u043D\u043E\u04:
1. Install a Python version supported by argostranslate, then run python -m pip install argostranslate in a terminal. If Python 3.14 dependencies fail, try a separate Python 3.11 or 3.12.

2. In Languages → Interface language and translation models enter that same python.exe path. Click Check Argos. A missing-module error means argostranslate was installed into another Python.

3. Download a .argosmodel with the correct direction. ru → en translates Russian to English; ar → en translates Arabic to English and does not substitute for ru → en. Reverse translation needs a separate package.

4. Click Install .argosmodel…, select the downloaded file, and check the installed-model list. In the Translate text block choose Local Argos and the source/target codes. FR/ES/ZH help translation needs ru → the selected interface language.

The LibreTranslate check contacts a separate server, initially 127.0.0.1:5000; Kliker Blocks does not start it. A connection error means no server is listening there. Local Argos does not need that server. Detect language and If translation available currently do require LibreTranslate. Install models only from trusted sources.
sections.\u0412\u043E\u0437\u043C\u043E\u0436\u04: At first launch, Kliker Blocks saves a local inventory to %LOCALAPPDATA%\KLIKER Blocks\computer-capabilities.json: Windows and .NET versions, architecture, UI and keyboard languages, installed voices and display bounds. If that folder is not writable, the file is saved beside Kliker.Blocks.exe; the window shows the actual path. It does not record the user name, document paths or installed programs and does not upload the file. Open Languages → Computer and voices to inspect or refresh it after adding a voice or display. Voices are not downloaded automatically. For Speak text, leave Voice blank: Russian and Chinese script select matching voices, other text uses the system default. Russian text needs a ru voice, such as Irina or Pavel; English Zira cannot read it properly. Add a missing voice in Windows language settings. Stopping the scenario interrupts speech playback.

blocks.Start: Entry point. A project needs exactly one Start block. Connect Next to the first action.
blocks.ShowcaseStep: Internal step of the What I can do demo graph. Action selects a built-in demo operation; Caption labels the node. Running an exported graph requires consent. Stop interrupts pending actions, but opened windows and files remain and clipboard content may have changed. Requires a Kliker Blocks build that supports this demo.
blocks.Description: Background label for a group of blocks. It does not execute and has no connectors. Drag its top bar or border to move it, or its lower-right corner to resize it. Set caption, size, #RRGGBB color and opacity (0–100%) in properties. Blocks inside are not attached to it.
blocks.WatchCursor: Returns the system cursor when it moves from its anchor. Activation can be immediate, toggled, or active while a key is held; a mouse button can be required too. Assign keys by pressing them in the capture dialog. The indicator is red while waiting and green when toggled on. Example: F9 plus left mouse button. Duration 0 means until stopped in one-pass mode, or one check per pass in repeating mode.
blocks.MoveCursor: Moves the system cursor once using SetCursorPos: to the monitor center, absolute X/Y, an offset from its current position, or an offset from the monitor center. Offsets can be negative. For applications reading relative motion, use Move mouse relatively instead.
blocks.MoveRelative: Sends a relative movement with Windows SendInput. Positive X moves right; positive Y moves down. Delay postpones the start. Duration 0 or one step sends the whole motion at once; multiple steps distribute the exact total ΔX/ΔY across the duration. For one action per key press, use If key down → On new press. For repeated motion while held, choose While held and Repeat until stopped. A second block with negative deltas can reverse the motion after a Wait. This does not measure or set a game's camera position. Stop with Ctrl+Alt+F7. Use macros only where permitted.
blocks.Click: Presses and releases the left, right or middle button at the current pointer position, 1–100 times. To hold or drag, use Mouse button Down → Move cursor → Mouse button Up.
blocks.MouseButton: Presses or releases a mouse button. Kliker Blocks releases buttons it holds when the scenario ends or stops. Corresponds to LDOWN/LUP, RDOWN/RUP and MDOWN/MUP.
blocks.Wheel: Scrolls the wheel up or down by 1–100 steps. Corresponds to WHEELUP/WHEELDOWN.
blocks.Key: Briefly presses a key. Supported names include A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, ENTER, SPACE, TAB, ESC, CTRL, ALT, SHIFT, BACKSPACE, arrows, HOME, END, DELETE, INSERT, PAGEUP, PAGEDOWN and WIN. Corresponds to KEYPRESS.
blocks.KeyState: Presses or releases a key across blocks, for example CTRL down → A → CTRL up. Kliker Blocks releases keys it still holds on stop. Corresponds to KEYDOWN/KEYUP.
blocks.VirtualKey: Presses or releases a key by decimal Windows VK code (1–255). Examples: 13=Enter, 17=Ctrl, 18=Alt, 27=Esc, 32=Space, 46=Delete, 65=A, 90=Z, 112=F1, 118=F7. Its name appears below the entered code. Open the searchable VK code table for all codes. OEM keys depend on layout; macro recording can capture passwords.
blocks.TypeText: Sends Unicode characters to the active window through Windows SendInput; no keyboard-layout change is needed. The target must accept ordinary system input.
blocks.ClipboardSet: Places text on the Windows clipboard. To paste it, add CTRL down → V → CTRL up blocks.
blocks.ClipboardGet: Stores clipboard text in a variable, or an empty string if no text is present. Copy in the target application first if needed.
blocks.TextFile: Works with UTF-8 text files: read, count, replace or insert a numbered line, append, overwrite with one line, delete a line, clear or delete the file. Line numbers start at 1. Insertion past the end appends. Paths are relative to the project folder. Reading/editing is limited to 8 MiB; deletion does not require reading the contents.
blocks.TextFileArray: TFREADARR reads a UTF-8 file into an array, replacing old entries; TFWRITEARR writes one element per line. Indices start at 0; missing sparse items become 0 in the file. The result variable receives the line count. Limits: 10000 lines and 8 MiB. Elements containing newlines cannot be written.
blocks.IniFile: Reads or writes a key in an INI section. A missing section/key reads as an empty string. Writing creates them if needed. The result is placed in a variable.
blocks.DirectoryList: Lists files or directories matching a wildcard such as *.txt. Supply directory and mask separately, or a path containing * or ? as with GETFILELIST/GETDIRLIST. Array items are names without the directory, indexed from 0. The result variable receives the count. Old array entries are removed. Limit: 10000 entries; no recursive traversal.
blocks.HttpGet: Performs an HTTP/HTTPS GET and stores the UTF-8 response in a variable. Optional headers are one Name: value per line, up to 32 and 8192 characters total. Fields support ${variable}. Timeout: 100–60000 ms; response limit: 8 MiB. HTTP errors stop the scenario. Use trusted URLs: addresses and headers may contain sensitive data.
blocks.TranslateText: Translates phrases and sentences. By default it needs a running LibreTranslate /translate service; localhost:5000 without one fails. A remote service receives the submitted text. For offline use, click Download offline language pair in this block, confirm installation, then select Argos local. Source must be explicit rather than auto; supported codes are ru, en, fr, es, zh and de, subject to installed models. Text supports ${variable} or =expression; output goes to a variable. Limit: 16000 characters, timeout 100–60000 ms.
blocks.DetectLanguage: Uses LibreTranslate /detect and writes the language code and confidence to two variables. Requires a running server; local Argos alone does not provide this operation. Connection errors stop the scenario.
blocks.LanguagePair: Checks whether the selected source can reach the target. Choose LibreTranslate to query a running service's /languages, or Argos local to check installed models; the latter needs the optional offline engine. Takes Yes or No. A service connection or local engine error stops the scenario.
blocks.TranslateArray: Translates up to 500 array strings sequentially through a connected LibreTranslate service by default. Use Download offline language pair to install optional Argos models, then choose Argos local with an explicit source code. The destination array and count update only after success; an error leaves the original result unchanged. Each item has its own timeout; stopping cancels the rest.
blocks.Wait: Waits 0–3,600,000 milliseconds (WAITMS); stopping interrupts it. This runs only when execution reaches this block. To delay cursor return, connect If cursor moved: Yes → Wait → Move cursor. Wait connected to Repeat: Next runs only after all repetitions.
blocks.InputGroup: An atomic group sharing the input queue for mouse, keyboard, clipboard and active window. Connect Body to the first action and end it with Branch end; then Next runs. Example: click a field, then type text. The lock is released on completion, stop, error or timeout (100–60000 ms). Avoid long waits inside. Parallel is not allowed in a group. Individual actions also acquire the queue while they run.
blocks.SetVariable: Creates or replaces a variable. Names use A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and _, beginning with a letter or _. Values can be text, a number, ${other_value} or =expression. Names are case-insensitive; the value lasts through the current run.
blocks.DefineVariable: Creates a variable with an initial value only if it does not exist. Existing values remain unchanged. It is useful for a counter that must persist across scenario passes.
blocks.UndefineVariable: Deletes the variable and same-named array (UNDEFINE). Reading it afterward yields 0; DEFINE can recreate it. Computed $_ system variables are unaffected.
blocks.SetVariableByName: SETVAR changes an existing scalar variable using a name supplied as a string, for example $counter or ${reference} containing $counter. Value supports =expression. A missing target is an error; Set variable or DEFINE creates one. Use =getvar($reference) to read indirectly.
blocks.MathVariable: Adds, subtracts, multiplies or divides a numeric variable. A missing value starts at 0. Operands can use ${other_variable}; fractional values are supported. Division by zero or nonnumeric input reports an error.
blocks.ArraySet: Writes an array element at index 0–1000000. Names follow the variable-name rule. Index and value can start with = for expressions. Read with =$items[0] or =$items[$i]. A missing item reads as 0.
blocks.ArrayAction: Appends, pops the last element, gets size, or sorts as text, numbers or automatically. Automatic sorting is numeric only if all elements are numeric. Popping an empty array returns 0. Expressions support arrsize($items) and arrpop($items). A sparse array's size is its highest index plus one. Arrays last for the run.
blocks.StringSplit: Splits a string on an exact delimiter (STRSEPARATE), replacing the destination array. Indices begin at 0 and empty segments are retained. A count variable receives the number of parts. Delimiter cannot be empty; maximum 10000 parts. String and delimiter support ${variable} or =expression.
blocks.IfVariable: Tests an existing variable. Equals, not equals and contains compare text case-insensitively; greater/less compare numbers. Comparison input can use ${name}. Branches: Yes and No.
blocks.IfExpression: Evaluates a field beginning with =. Zero takes No; nonzero takes Yes. Expressions support $variable, $array[index], arithmetic, parentheses, comparisons, and/or/xor/not, rnd, sqrt, strlen and other functions. Use it for complex conditions.
blocks.WhileExpression: Repeats Body while its =expression is nonzero, reevaluating after each iteration. End Body with Branch end; Next runs when false. The iteration cap prevents accidental endless loops; 0 removes that cap. Stop interrupts the loop.
blocks.SwitchValue: Compares a value against five options in order and follows the first match. Empty options are skipped; Otherwise runs if none match. Fields accept =expressions. Numbers compare numerically; other text ignores case. Chain Otherwise to another Switch for more options.
blocks.IfMoved: Checks the cursor distance from its anchor once. Yes means outside the threshold. For a delayed return connect Yes → Wait → Move cursor; for continuous monitoring use Watch cursor.
blocks.IfPixel: Captures one screen pixel and compares it with a color. Tolerance applies to each R/G/B channel (0 is exact). Yes means a match. The measured color is logged.
blocks.WaitPixel: Repeatedly checks one pixel until its color matches or a timeout expires. Set the polling interval in milliseconds. Timeout 0 waits until stopped. Outputs are Found and Timeout.
blocks.IfKeyDown: Checks a key or mouse button. While held yields Yes each pass; On new press yields Yes once per physical press; Toggle changes a stored state on each new press. Repeating scenarios test on each pass. Press-to-assign captures keys or mouse buttons; LMB/RMB/MMB or decimal VK codes can be entered manually. While held corresponds to ISKEYDOWN.
blocks.FindColor: Finds the first pixel of a given color in a rectangle. Outputs Found/No. Its coordinates are logged and available to Move to found point in the same branch. Corresponds to IF_PIXEL_IN.
blocks.FindImage: Finds a BMP/PNG template on screen within bounds. Tolerance 0–255 applies per color channel; fully transparent PNG pixels are ignored. Returns the match's top-left corner. Large images/regions can be slow; protected output may not be capturable. Corresponds to IF_PICTURE_IN.
blocks.Screenshot: Saves a rectangular screen area as PNG, creating the destination folder if needed. The whole rectangle must be inside the virtual desktop.
blocks.BufferCapture: Stores a screen snapshot for later analysis blocks, either the full virtual desktop or a rectangle. Left/top bounds are inclusive; right/bottom are exclusive. A new capture replaces the previous one; repeated checks otherwise see the same pixels. Corresponds to GETSCREEN.
blocks.BufferPixel: Reads one pixel from the stored snapshot into a variable. Coordinates are screen coordinates. COLORREF is decimal R + G×256 + B×65536; #RRGGBB is also available. Capture screen first.
blocks.BufferCount: Counts pixels matching a color in an area of the stored snapshot. Tolerance 0–255 applies separately to R/G/B. Writes a result variable. Corresponds to PXLCOUNT. Capture again for fresh pixels.
blocks.BufferHash: Computes XOR or CRC32 of RGB pixels in a stored-snapshot region and writes an unsigned result. Compare the same region across captures. CRC32 reads R,G,B bytes left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
blocks.BufferReplace: Changes a color in the stored snapshot, not on the physical screen. Old color -1 means any color. Writes the changed-pixel count. Use Save snapshot to inspect the result. Corresponds to PXLREPLACE.
blocks.BufferFindColor: Finds the first matching pixel in the stored snapshot. Branches Found/No; coordinates go to Move to found point and $_return1/$_return2. Capture screen first.
blocks.BufferFindImage: Finds a PNG/BMP/JPG template in the stored snapshot. Writes its top-left coordinates to $_return1/$_return2 for Move to found point. Fully transparent pixels and an optional background color are ignored. Tolerance is separate for R/G/B. Capture first.
blocks.BufferScanColor: Finds every matching-color pixel in the stored snapshot up to the chosen limit. Replaces an array with X,Y pairs: [0]=X, [1]=Y, [2]=X, [3]=Y, and writes the number of points. Order is top-to-bottom, left-to-right. Corresponds to single-color SCANPXL.
blocks.BufferScanImage: Finds every template location in the stored snapshot, including overlaps, up to the chosen limit. Replaces an array with X,Y pairs and writes a count. Transparency/background color excludes template pixels. Tolerance 0–255 applies per channel, not as a percentage.
blocks.BufferSave: Saves the current stored snapshot, including Replace color edits, to a PNG file. It does not capture the screen again. Relative paths start in the saved project's folder.
blocks.MoveFound: Moves the cursor to the last point found by Find color/image in the same branch, plus an offset. If no point exists, the scenario errors. For a template's center, offset by half its width and height.
blocks.IfWindow: Finds a visible window by a case-insensitive title substring. Yes if found, otherwise No. With multiple matches, Windows enumeration order determines the first.
blocks.ActivateWindow: Finds a visible window by title substring, restores it and tries to activate it. Windows may prevent background activation; an elevated target may require Kliker Blocks to run elevated.
blocks.MoveWindow: Finds a visible window by title substring and sets X/Y and dimensions in screen pixels. Width/height must be positive. Elevated targets may require corresponding permissions.
blocks.WindowFind: Finds a visible window by title substring or prefix and writes its numeric HWND, or 0 if none. The first match is returned. HWND becomes stale after the window closes.
blocks.WindowInfo: Reads a window's screen X, Y, width and height from numeric HWND into four variables. An invalid HWND is an error. Corresponds to WNDGETINFO.
blocks.WindowAction: Acts on numeric HWND: set position, size, full geometry, state (0 minimize, 1 restore), or activate. Windows may reject changes to another process. Corresponds to WNDPOS, WNDSIZE, WNDSETINFO, WNDSTATE and WNDBUMP.
blocks.ElementAtPoint: Returns the numeric HWND of the Windows element at screen X/Y, or 0 if none. Coordinates accept expressions or the current mouse position. Corresponds to HGET(x,y).
blocks.ElementInfo: Reads a standard Windows element's text or process PID by HWND into a variable. WM_GETTEXT has a 500 ms timeout and 4096-character cap; custom controls may return no text. Corresponds to HGETTEXT/HGETPID.
blocks.ElementSetText: Sends WM_SETTEXT to an element by HWND, with a 500 ms timeout and 4096-character cap. Windows may reject cross-process writes; custom controls may not support it. Corresponds to HSETTEXT.
blocks.MessageSend: Sends a numeric message code (0–65535) to an HWND. Asynchronous POSTMESSAGE returns 1 when queued. Synchronous SENDMESSAGE waits up to 500 ms and writes the result. wParam/lParam accept integers only, not pointers or strings. Avoid unknown codes in other applications.
blocks.MessageReceive: Reads the last WM_USER (1024) wParam/lParam sent to this Kliker Blocks instance's main window. The new-message flag is 1 once, then 0 until another arrives. Use $_hwnd_self for your window. Instances do not mix messages.
blocks.RunFile: Launches an .exe, .bat, .cmd, .lnk shortcut, document or associated file through Windows. Click Choose a program or file to search installed Start-menu programs, or Browse files to select any existing file; you can still type a path. Relative paths resolve from the project folder. Arguments are passed as text. Optionally wait for exit with a timeout. If a shortcut launches without returning a process handle, waiting is unavailable. Exit codes, when available, are logged.
blocks.RunAhk: Runs an .ahk script with AutoHotkey v2. Enter script path and optionally AutoHotkey64.exe/AutoHotkey32.exe v2 path. An empty interpreter field searches standard installation folders. Arguments, wait and timeout are configurable. AHK v1 scripts are unsupported.
blocks.RunScenario: Runs a saved .klb scenario sequentially after this block. Select a file, 1–1000 repetitions and 0.1–5.0× speed. The child always runs a single pass; explicit feedback cycles are rejected so the repeat count is meaningful. Stopping the parent stops the child. Nesting is limited to eight levels; variables are separate.
blocks.Repeat: Executes Body the specified number of times, then Next once. Next is not an inter-iteration pause: put Wait inside Body and end Body with Branch end. For up to 100 repetitions the journal shows each iteration. Maximum count is 100000.
blocks.CallSub: Calls a named Subroutine start. On Return from subroutine or an unconnected output, execution continues at this block's Next. Names match case-insensitively; definitions must be unique. Maximum nested call depth is 32.
blocks.SubStart: Starts a named subroutine. Place it separately from the main chain, choose a unique name, connect Body to its first action and finish with Return from subroutine. Call it through Call subroutine only.
blocks.SubReturn: Equivalent to END_SUB. Ends the called subroutine and resumes at the caller's Next. It is an error outside a subroutine.
blocks.Parallel: Starts branches A and B concurrently, waits for both, then follows Next. End each branch with Branch end. Input actions are queued to prevent mixed simultaneous keys/clicks.
blocks.BranchEnd: Ends the current repeat or parallel branch. It also ends execution in an ordinary chain.
blocks.Log: Writes text to the execution journal. If Log file ran earlier, it appends that text to its UTF-8 file. Full journal-to-file recording is a separate Scenario setting. Log actions also records execution of this block.
blocks.LogFile: Duplicates later PRINT/LOGWRITE and Message block output to a UTF-8 file in the project folder. Enter only a filename, up to 160 characters. The file is created when this block runs, even if no message follows; its full path appears in the journal. Empty disables output. Appends across runs; limit 8 MiB. LOGCLEAR does not clear this file.
blocks.LogClear: Clears the visible built-in journal. With no UI attached, continues without effect. Corresponds to LOGCLEAR().
blocks.LogShow: Shows or hides the built-in journal panel: 1 show, 0 hide. The Scenario menu can open it manually. Separate LOGSHOW window coordinates are not supported.
blocks.PlaySound: Starts a WAV file asynchronously and continues. A relative path is resolved against the project folder. Missing or invalid WAV files report errors. Corresponds to SOUND(file).
blocks.SpeakText: Speaks text with modern installed Windows voices. Text supports ${variable} and =expression, so it can read results from earlier blocks. Leave Voice blank for automatic selection by text language (ru for Cyrillic, zh for Chinese); the picker lists voice languages. Selecting a voice of the wrong language reports an error instead of silent speech. Rate is -10 to 10, volume 0–100, text at most 16000 characters. The block waits for speech to finish; stopping the scenario interrupts playback. Put it in a parallel branch for concurrent work. Voices depend on Windows; speech does not translate text.
blocks.Beep: Plays a system tone at 37–32767 Hz for 1–5000 ms, then continues. If the old Windows Beep API is unsupported, playback falls back to the normal audio device. If both fail, the error is logged. Corresponds to BEEP(freq,time).
blocks.InputDialog: Shows a text prompt and saves the answer to a variable. The default is returned if time expires before input starts; timeout 0 waits indefinitely. Cancel returns an empty string. Timeout is 0–3600 seconds, default 5. Stopping closes the dialog. Corresponds to INPUTBOX(message,default[,delay]).
blocks.ChoiceDialog: Shows a question. Choose the visible button set by name: 0 OK; 1 OK/Cancel; 2 Abort/Retry/Ignore; 3 Yes/No/Cancel; 4 Yes/No; 5 Retry/Cancel. A set number is NOT a result code: Yes returns 6 and No returns 7. The selected set's result codes appear under the field. The icon is also chosen by name. Stopping closes the dialog. Corresponds to DIALOGBOX(message,buttons[,icon]).
blocks.RadioDialog: Shows one choice per line (1–100 choices, up to 250 characters each). OK returns the chosen 1-based index; cancel or OK without a selection returns 0. Stopping closes the dialog.
blocks.HintPopup: Requests a Windows notification with message and title, then continues. It uses the Kliker Blocks tray icon; Windows settings may hide or delay it. Corresponds to HINTPOPUP(message[,title]).
blocks.Stop: Stops the whole scenario, including parallel branches after their current action. External processes already started remain running.
